resources.string: Menu names are those of the official firmware in English.
Builds HiByOS %1$s from the official firmware of your HiBy R3 II (2025) and puts it on the player.
Already running the official firmware v%1$s
Micro SD card in the player
The player must stay on during the update
How to check the firmware version
Your HiBy R3 II (2025) must already be running the official firmware v%1$s. On any other version, update it to the official v%1$s first.
Get the official firmware v%1$s from HiBy
Add HiByOS to it, on this phone
Over Wi-Fi, or by hand with the SD card
Start the update on the player
This app contains no HiBy firmware. You start from your own copy of the official firmware: the app downloads it from HiBy, or you choose the file yourself.
HiByOS is installed on top of HiBy\'s official firmware v%1$s. Use this app only with a HiBy R3 II (2025) that is already running that version.
Check the version on the player
On the player\'s home screen, open **System**.
Scroll down the list and open **About**.
Read the firmware version. It must be **%1$s**.
Read the line that starts with **BuildTime**. The official v%1$s shows **%2$s**.
Put a micro SD card in the player and connect the player to Wi-Fi.
On the home screen, open **System › Firmware update** and choose **Via OTA**. Install the official v%1$s.
Or get the official v%1$s file from HiBy\'s page, copy **%2$s** to the top level of the SD card and choose **Via SD-card** in the same menu.
If the player is on, or offers, a version newer than v%1$s, this version of the app does not support it: look for a newer HiByOS Install.
HiByOS keeps its apps and files in a **HiByOS** folder on the card. Use a card the player already reads, with at least 100 MB free, and leave it in the player.
The official firmware is not included in this app. It comes from HiBy\'s own download link, or from a copy you already have.
Choose a file on this phone
Download it with the browser, then choose it here
The file is checked (SHA-256) before it is used. Only the exact official v%1$s is accepted.
Checked: it is the exact file published by HiBy.
This is not the official firmware v%1$s
The app only accepts **%1$s** exactly as HiBy publishes it for the R3 II (2025). The file you chose is another version, for another model, or was changed.
The app opens your firmware file, adds the HiByOS files and settings, builds it again and checks every file of the result. Everything happens on this phone and takes about a minute.
Keep the app open until it finishes.
What goes on the SD card
The HiByOS firmware you just built · %1$s
Both go to the top level of the player\'s SD card.
How do you want to send them?
With the player\'s own “Import Music via Wi-Fi”. No cables, no card reader.
Save the files and copy them to the card with a card reader or a computer.
Both ways give the same result. If Wi-Fi gives trouble, the manual way always works.
On the player\'s home screen, open **Wireless › Wi-Fi**, turn Wi-Fi on and join the same network as this phone.
Go back to **Wireless** and open **Import Music via Wi-Fi**.
The player shows **Receive songs via Wi-Fi** and an address like **http://192.168.1.20:%1$d**. Keep that screen open until the app has finished.
Menu names are those of the official firmware in English. Music stops while that screen is open.
Type the address, or let the app look for the player: “Find my player” asks the devices of your own Wi-Fi network, on port %1$d only, which one is the player.
Keep the player on its Wi-Fi screen and this app open. The firmware goes last, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a half update on the card.
Everything is on the SD card
%1$d files are on the card; %2$d were read back and compared.
%1$d files are on the card. Their sizes were checked; the player did not allow reading them back.
Get the files out of the app
The SD card in a reader connected to this phone, or any folder
Send %1$s and HiByOS.zip to a computer or another app
If you choose the top level of the player\'s SD card, everything lands in the right place at once.
%1$s and the HiByOS folder (%2$d files), each one checked after writing.
The card needs **%1$s** and the **HiByOS** folder at the top level, not inside another folder.
If you shared **HiByOS.zip**, unpack it: the card needs the folder, not the zip.
If the card already has a file called **%1$s**, replace it.
Eject the card safely and put it back in the player.
The files are on the card
The SD card is in the player, with **%1$s** and the **HiByOS** folder at the top level.
The player is running the official firmware v%1$s.
If the **Receive songs via Wi-Fi** screen is still open, leave it.
Go to the home screen and open **System › Firmware update**.
Choose **Via SD-card** and confirm **Update system firmware?**
Wait. The player installs the update and restarts by itself. Do not switch it off.
HiByOS starts and finishes setting itself up from the card. Keep the **HiByOS** folder on the card from now on.
If the player says “No firmware update file found!”, it does not see %1$s at the top level of the card.
To return to the official firmware at any time, put HiBy\'s original **%1$s** on the card and install it the same way.
Removes the downloaded firmware and the built file from the app
You have the latest HiByOS files (%1$s).
HiByOS %1$s is now in the app. Build it in step 2.
Newer HiByOS files come from the project\'s releases on GitHub. They are accepted only if they are signed with the project\'s release key and match their SHA-256.
What the app sends over the network
**HiBy\'s download link** (Google Drive): only when you tap “Download from HiBy”.
**GitHub**: only when you tap “Check for newer HiByOS files”.
**Your player**, on your own Wi-Fi network: only when you use the Wi-Fi way.
No accounts, no ads, no analytics. The app sends nothing about you or your devices to anyone.
Removes the downloaded firmware and the built file (%1$s)
HiByOS is an independent community project, not affiliated with HiBy. This app contains no HiBy firmware. Installing unofficial software on your player is at your own risk.

Check the internet connection and try again: the download continues where it stopped.
HiBy\'s link did not send the file
Try again later. Or open HiBy\'s download page, download the file with the browser and choose it here.
The downloaded file is not the official firmware
The file could not be written
Check the free space on this phone and try again.
Not enough free space on this phone
The file could not be read
Get the firmware again in step 1.
The HiByOS files cannot be used
Update HiByOS Install to its latest version.
HiByOS does not fit in the player
The result did not pass its check
Nothing was produced. Try again; if it happens again, please report it on the project page.
Check that the player still shows “Receive songs via Wi-Fi”, that both devices are on the same Wi-Fi network, and that the address is the one on its screen.
That address is not the player
Type the address shown on the player\'s “Receive songs via Wi-Fi” screen.
The player has no SD card it can use
Put a micro SD card in the player, leave “Import Music via Wi-Fi” and open it again.
The card may be full or write-protected. Free some space (100 MB) and try again, or use the manual way.
The connection to the player broke
Keep the player on its Wi-Fi screen and near the router, then try again: files that already arrived are not sent twice.
A file did not arrive intact
Try again. If it keeps happening, use the manual way.
A file on this phone could not be read
That does not look like an address
Type the numbers the player shows, for example 192.168.1.20
No player found on this Wi-Fi network
Make sure the player shows “Receive songs via Wi-Fi” and is on the same Wi-Fi as this phone. Guest networks often keep devices apart: then type the address by hand, or use the manual way.
This phone is not on a Wi-Fi network
Connect this phone to the same Wi-Fi network as the player.
The newer HiByOS files were not accepted
The app keeps using the files it has.
The check could not be made
Check the internet connection and try again.
The files could not be saved there
Choose another folder, or check that the card is not full or write-protected.
The files could not be prepared
No app on this phone can open that
